live.name: ALPHV
live.headline: ALPHV: a ransomware actor known by several names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists ALPHV under several aliases and a set of tools. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: ALPHV is the main name for this actor in the catalogue record.
It is also listed as ALPHVM, Ambitious Scorpius, BlackCat Gang and UNC4466.
The catalogue links the name to tools including BlackCat, Noberus, Munchkin, Mimikatz, Impacket, PsExec, LaZagne, MEGAsync and GO Simple Tunnel (GOST).
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: ALPHV
next.headline: ALPHV (BlackCat): a ransomware-as-a-service gang built on leak-site extortion
next.in_short: ALPHV, also called BlackCat, ran a ransomware-as-a-service operation. Reports describe leak-site extortion against firms from software to healthcare, with many figures resting on the gang's own claims.

sentences.t: The catalogue lists ALPHV under several other names: ALPHVM, Ambitious Scorpius, BlackCat Gang and UNC4466.
Sygnia says the BlackCat group surfaced in November 2021 and uses a ransomware-as-a-service model, in which affiliates carry out attacks.
BleepingComputer reports that the operation is believed to be a rebrand of the DarkSide and BlackMatter gangs.
BleepingComputer also cites an estimate that BlackCat took in at least $300 million in ransom payments from more than 1,000 victims.
Sygnia describes BlackCat as targeting high-profile organisations across many sectors worldwide.
Named victims in the reports include Suffolk County's local government, the software firm Constellation Software, and the dental and medical distributor Henry Schein.
In a 2023 case Sygnia attributes to BlackCat or one of its affiliates, access came through a compromised third-party vendor. Sygnia does not name a single confirmed actor.
In that case the attacker used Cobalt Strike for lateral movement, and Rclone to copy data out. It then sent extortion emails to dozens of employees.
The gang posts victims on a leak site with deadlines. DataBreaches reported a 48-hour deadline and a claim of over 800 GB stolen from Hampton-Newport News CSB.
The catalogue lists tools tied to the group, including Mimikatz, Impacket, PsExec, LaZagne and MEGAsync.
Check Point Research lists BlackCat/ALPHV among the tools noted for Scattered Spider. ReliaQuest says Scattered Spider has alliances with ALPHV and other ransomware operators.
In September 2022 a ransomware attack disabled Suffolk County's 911 system. DataBreaches reports that BlackCat claimed it and said it held 400 GB of data. DataBreaches could not confirm the leak.
In May 2023 ALPHV claimed on its leak site to have stolen more than 1 TB from Constellation Software.
In a statement on the MGM Resorts attack, AlphV said it launched ransomware against more than 100 ESXi hypervisors on September 11. These are the group's own unverified claims.
In July 2023 ALPHV was listed as a victim-poster for Estée Lauder. The report says BlackCat claimed over 130 GB stolen without encrypting the network, which is the hackers' own claim.
Henry Schein disclosed an incident on October 15, 2023. The report says AlphV claimed it and re-encrypted systems after negotiations broke down.
In December 2023 DataBreaches reported an unconfirmed AlphV claim about Viking Therapeutics. The claim was that an employee was intimidated into filing an SEC complaint.

In February 2024 unnamed sources told BleepingComputer the Change Healthcare attack was linked to BlackCat. BleepingComputer could not confirm this. UnitedHealth's SEC filing blamed a suspected nation-state actor.
BleepingComputer reports the FBI temporarily took down BlackCat's negotiation and leak sites in December.
SecurityScorecard says RansomHub was likely filling the vacuum left by AlphV/BlackCat's disbanding.
Treat a leak-site claim as unverified until the victim confirms it.
Limit and monitor third-party vendor access, and keep backups that an intruder cannot reach.
